parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Benzene reacts with D in the presence of a suitable catalyst to give cumene and non-organic product E. This is an electrophilic substitution reaction.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Name the reactant D and the non-organic product E.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Give the name of the type of aromatic electrophilic substitution reaction taking place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Cumene undergoes substitution reactions with chlorine to give several different isomeric products with the formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$. The substitution can occur in the aromatic ring or in the side-chain of cumene.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Describe the conditions that are used to ensure substitution takes place only in the aromatic ring.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the structures of the two major isomeric products of the reaction, formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$, when substitution takes place in the aromatic ring.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Describe the conditions that are used to ensure substitution takes place only in the side-chain.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Draw the structures of two isomeric products of the reaction, formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$, when substitution takes place in the side-chain.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Cumene can be nitrated using a mixture of concentrated nitric and sulfuric acids. The mechanism for this reaction is similar to the mechanism for the nitration of benzene.

Complete the mechanism for this reaction.

- Include all relevant charges and curly arrows showing the movement of electron pairs.
- Draw the structure of the intermediate.
- You do not need to draw the products.
